def: A translation unit that contains a *module-declaration* (`export module M;`, `module M:P;`, etc.).
The collection of all module units with the same *module-name*. Dots in a module name carry no hierarchical meaning.
A module unit whose *module-declaration* begins with `export`; `export` declarations can appear only in its purview.

A module unit that is not an interface unit (`module M;` or an implementation partition `module M:P;`). It cannot be exported; an implementation unit without a partition name cannot be imported and implicitly imports the primary interface unit.
The module interface unit without a partition name; each named module has exactly one (IFNDR if violated). Interface partitions must be exported by it directly or indirectly.

A module unit whose *module-declaration* contains `:P`, divided into interface partitions and implementation partitions; it can be imported only by units of the same module with `import :P;`, and is invisible outside the module.

The purview of a module unit is the token sequence from the *module-declaration* to the end of the TU (excluding the global module fragment, including the private module fragment); the purview of a named module is the set of purviews of all its module units.
The collection of all global module fragments and all non-module TUs (including header units); it has no name and no interface unit. Declarations in traditional code are all attached to it.

Every declaration is attached to one module: declarations of namespaces, of type/namespace aliases, and within a language linkage specification are attached to the global module; a friend that names an existing entity follows the named entity; the rest follow the purview they appear in. Same-named entities attached to different modules are different entities.

A declaration within an *export-declaration* that inhabits a namespace scope, a namespace definition containing an exported declaration, or a declaration in a header unit that introduces a name. Name lookup in importers can find it; it cannot declare a name with internal linkage (except in header units).

A TU imported by `import <h>;` or `import "h";`, synthesized from an importable header via translation phases 1–7: it has an independent macro environment, all its declarations are implicitly exported and attached to the global module, and its macros are visible to direct importers.
An implementation-defined set of headers that can be imported as header units, including at least all importable C++ library headers (Table 24 in [[headers]]).

A TU has an interface dependency on U if it imports U (including the implicit import by a *module-declaration*), or has an interface dependency on some TU that depends on U. A TU must not have an interface dependency on itself (circular imports are prohibited).

The part of a module unit between `module;` and the *module-declaration*, which may contain only preprocessing directives; the declarations in it (via `#include`) are attached to the global module, and those not used by the purview are discarded.

A relation between declarations in the same TU: D is mentioned by S, named by an expression in S, found by conservative lookup for a dependent call in S, etc., closed under rules for classes and members, templates and specializations, and so on. Used to determine whether declarations in the global module fragment are discarded.
A declaration in the global module fragment that is not decl-reachable from any declaration in the TU's *declaration-seq*. It is neither reachable nor visible outside that module unit.

The part after `module :private;`, which may appear only in a primary interface unit that is the module's only unit; declarations in it are not reachable from other TUs and are not subject to exposure checks.

The set of program points that determines which declarations ADL for dependent names can find and which declarations are reachable; for nested instantiations it includes the end of the module's primary interface unit.
A TU that is necessarily reachable from a point P: a module interface unit on which the TU containing P has an interface dependency before P, or a TU directly imported before P.

The semantic properties of a declaration (definition, completeness, default arguments, etc.) take effect at a point. A declaration is reachable from P if it precedes P in the same TU, or is in a reachable TU, is not discarded, and is not in a private module fragment. Unrelated to whether it is exported.
